paragraphs.source_en: When they were all out, they stood staring at each other: the six refugees, Michel and Iwao, and two younger drivers, one man and one woman. The ten of them set off on foot, in darkness, using headlamps only during the tricky climb down the broken-off section of the road ramp. Once back on the road, they turned their headlamps off and strode down the steeply sloping gravel path, falling naturally into the long lope that was the most comfortable pace in this angle of descent. The night was starless, and the wind whistled downcanyon around them, sometimes in gusts so strong that it felt like they were being shoved in the back. It felt like another dust storm was indeed beginning; Sax muttered about equatorial versus global, but it was impossible to tell what it would be. "Let's hope it goes global," Michel said. "We can use the cover."
